 ORDER

This petition is filed by the Jabalpur Development Authority, being aggrieved of the order dated 23.06.2009, passed by learned Second Additional District Judge, Jabalpur (M.P.), in Execution Case No.27/2008 (Ramesh Prasad Yadav Vs. Jabalpur Development Authority), directing the authorities to refund amount of income tax deducted by them on payment of compensation which was due to the decree holder on account of acquisition of his agricultural land.

sentences.text: Provided that no deduction shall be made under this section where the amount of such payment or, as the case may be, the aggregate amount of such payments to a resident during the financial year does not exceed Rs.2,50,000/-."

3. Reading from the definition of agricultural land in India as provided in Section 2(14)(iii) of the Act of 1961, it is pointed out that agricultural land in India is one which is not being a land situate - (a) in any area which is comprised within the jurisdiction of a municipality (whether known as a municipality, municipal corporation, notified area committee, town area committee, town committee, or by any other name) or a cantonment board and which has a population of not less than ten thousand.

4. Thus, it is submitted that admittedly land of the judgment creditor being situated within the municipal limits of Jabalpur, he was not entitled to an exemption as is provided under Section 194LA of the Act of 1961, as that will not fall within the definition of agricultural land as an exception has been carved out while denying agricultural land in Section 2(14)(iii) of the Act of 1961.

5. Shri Siddharth Sharma, learned counsel for the Income Tax Department along with Shri Shiv Kumar, Joint Commissioner, Income Tax, submits that till yesterday he was counsel for Jabalpur Development Authority and on account of conflict of interest, he had made a request for engagement of another counsel when this Court was constrained to order for personal presence of the Commissioner, Income Tax.
He submits that yesterday evening, he has resigned from the panel of Jabalpur Development Authority and, therefore, he is now in a position to assist the Court.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, it is evident that while passing impugned order dated 23.06.2009, learned Second Additional District Judge, Jabalpur, has failed to take into consideration the definition of 'agricultural land in India' as defined in Section 2(14) (iii), inasmuch as, there are certain exceptions provided in the Act of 1961, for treating a land situated in the municipal area to be an agricultural land.
Thus, the order of refund of income tax is arbitrary, cryptic and deserves to be set aside and is hereby set aside.

7. At this stage, Shri Siddharth Sharma, submits that if respondent No.1 is interested in seeking refund of income tax, then the normal procedure is to file return and then after filing return refund Jabalpur Development Authority vs Ramesh Prasad Yadav on 7 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192116286/
2 is sought on the basis of an assessee not falling within the purview of the Act of 1961.

sentences.text: Thus, this order of learned Second Additional District Judge, Jabalpur, cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.

8. Taking aforesaid facts into consideration, this Court is of the opinion that the impugned order having been passed without authority and being oblivious of the provisions contained in Section 2(14)(iii) of the Act of 1961, cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.
Said order is, hereby, set aside.
9. In above terms, petition is allowed and disposed of.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) JUDGE A.Praj.
